name: Game_DriverContracts_OfferSecretMeeting
proto: void Game_DriverContracts_OfferSecretMeeting(void *contracts, const void *meeting, uint32_t team, uint32_t driver, uint8_t reason, uint8_t notify)
notes: Driver Career contracts manager (DriverCareerContractsManagerComponent): makes the driver's current secret meeting. Finds the driver's DriverSecretMeetings record in contracts+0x3a8..+0x3b0 (16-byte slots, record +0x40 driver key; returns when none). With notify set and the driver the human it posts ProcessSMMessage (vtable 0x145698190, name getter 0x140e04320; +0x10 driver, +0x14 meeting id, +0x18 team, +0x1c reason) through 0x140e0ab40. Then it allocates a 0x24-byte SecretMeeting from contracts+0x210 (vt+0x18, align 0x10), copies the 0x14-byte meeting definition (an entry of contracts+0x298..+0x2a0, 20 bytes) to +0x00, writes reason byte +0x14 = 3 (offered; a constant, not the argument), day +0x18 and weekend +0x1c (the definition's +0x04 percent of the season's weekends through the time component +0x370, 0x141267be0/0x141269000) and team +0x20; when the record already has a current meeting the new one is freed again (vt+0x38) and the old one stays, otherwise it is stored at record +0x18 with the allocator at +0x10 (0x140d7f7fe). Last it adds the meeting day to the career calendar through 0x141269180 (time component +0x370). Only two callers in the KB build: Game_DriverContracts_AdvanceSecretMeeting (0x140d8060f, the next meeting of a series) and 0x140d82710 (0x140d82aa1, after the contracts screen command 0x7388e27d marks the human's contract with removedReason 10); no other code allocates the 0x24 record except the save loader 0x140d730c0 and the online co-op receive 0x140d80630. Raised by laneS (Progressive Career lane S: secret meetings in follow mode).

name: Game_DriverContracts_AdvanceSecretMeeting
notes: Driver Career contracts manager: moves the driver's secret meetings on. Returns when the driver has no DriverSecretMeetings record (contracts+0x3a8..+0x3b0, record +0x40) or when his contract (contract_owner +0x298 list, DriverContract +0x50 driver) is active (+0x2c), its removedReason (+0x12) is not 10, it runs more than one season (+0x20 > 1) and does not end this season (+0x24 != time component +0x428). No current meeting (record +0x18 null): it takes the first meeting definition with id 0 (contracts+0x298..+0x2a0, 20-byte entries), picks a team with 0x140d7f830 (a random team of the driver's rank window, 0x140d80bc0) and calls Game_DriverContracts_OfferSecretMeeting(contracts, def, team, driver, 3, notify). A current meeting with reason (+0x14) 3 (offered, waiting for the player) is left alone. Any other reason (0 declined, 1 accepted, set by the secret meetings view model 0x1422fca00 just before its tail call) is resolved: 0x140d7fe80 works out the next definition id (reason 1 takes the definition's +0x08, 0 its +0x0c and adds the meeting's team to the ignored teams of the offers at contracts+0x3c8; it also updates the driver's 0x5c-byte entries of the component at contracts+0x380 (+0x460), and the reason 1 path ends in 0x14106bf60), the current meeting is moved onto the record's previous meetings (+0x28..+0x30) by 0x140d83cd0, which nulls record +0x18 (0x140d83d72/0x140d83db8), so the vt+0x38 free after it (0x140d803cf/0x140d8041b) finds nothing and the meeting lives on in the previous meetings; then the next definition, when one has that id, is offered (reason 3; a next definition with kind byte +0x10 == 0 after a non-accept gets a newly picked team, otherwise the meeting's team); with no such definition and notify set it posts ProcessSMMessage (vtable 0x145698190, meeting id -1) for the human. Callers: the daily tick 0x14126a1a0 (vtable 0x1456cdee8; its loop over contracts+0x3a8 calls 0x140d7f220 then this with notify 0 at 0x14126b899) and the secret meetings view model command handler 0x1422fca00 (vtable 0x14577dd20; commands 0xe47022a1 sets reason 0, 0xb027c7fd sets 1, then jmp here with notify 1 at 0x1422fcc89). Season change (contracts vtable +0x188, 0x140d76570) frees every current and previous meeting. Raised by laneS (Progressive Career lane S: secret meetings in follow mode).

name: Game_CareerActivities_AddActivity
proto: void Game_CareerActivities_AddActivity(void *calendar, const void *activity, uint32_t day)
notes: Adds a career calendar activity to one calendar (a driver's, 0xc8-byte objects in a season record's +0x40..+0x48, or a team's, 0xd8-byte objects in +0x60..+0x68): when the activity definition's mode mask (+0x60) allows the game mode (bit 1 Driver Career, bit 2 My Team, through Career_Is_MyTeamGameMode_Thunk on calendar +0x10), it creates the instance through the calendar's vtable +0x8 (calendar, out, activity, day) and +0x10 (calendar, activity id +0x08, day), then inserts it into the calendar's activity list (+0x48 allocator, +0x50..+0x58 16-byte slots {allocator, instance}) before the first instance whose day (+0x0a) is not earlier (0x1412c8320), or appends it (0x141289d50), and re-sorts (0x1412c70c0). The activity definition's type byte +0x10 indexes the names at 0x145731eb0 (0x0f NCSContractRenewal, the Driver Career contract event the Team HQ advance card shows as Team Select or Contract Negotiations; 0x10 NSCSSM the secret meeting). The daily tick 0x14126a1a0 adds the NCSContractRenewal definition (found by type 0x0f in the definitions map at +0x378..+0x388 of the activities component) to every driver and team calendar of the current season (0x14126bf46, 0x14126bf73); 24 call sites in all, e.g. the season populate 0x1412678d0 and the notification scheduler 0x141289690. Raised by laneS (Progressive Career follow mode: no contract event).

name: Game_CareerActivities_RemoveActivity
proto: void Game_CareerActivities_RemoveActivity(void *calendar, const void *activity, uint16_t day)
notes: The counterpart of Game_CareerActivities_AddActivity: removes from one calendar's activity list (+0x50..+0x58, 16-byte slots {allocator, instance}) the first instance of the matching class whose day (+0x0a, u16) is day and whose definition (+0x10) has the id (+0x08) of activity, destroying it (instance vtable +0x8, then the slot allocator's free), shifting the rest down and storing the new end (0x141267f63), then re-sorts the list. Callers: Career_ContractRenewal_RemoveEvent (0x140d8e37a, removing a renewal event from a human driver's calendar), the sponsor renewal view model 0x1423f6230 (0x1423f6577, after its event, on the calendar 0x14126f540 returns), the daily tick 0x14126a1a0 (0x14126bde9, 0x14126be19) 0x1412659e0/0x141265e40 and 0x140bf1e90 (0x140bf1f99); with no match it only re-sorts (V1099). Raised by laneS (Progressive Career follow mode: drop a saved contract event).

name: Sess_Assign_GarageSlotsByPreference
proto: void Sess_Assign_GarageSlotsByPreference(void *driver_registry, void *team_entrants, uint32_t garage_index, void *garages, void *out_assignments)
notes: cxx=assignGarageSlotsByPreference; every entrant of a team gets the same garage, slots 0,1,2... The garage is *(garages+8)[garage_index] read with no bound check (callers: Sess_Assign_GarageSlotsByTeamOrder's listed-team loop does not check it). The team's entrant with team_position present (EntrantRecord +0x81) and the lowest team_position (+0x80) looks up its driver (0x1423dbcf0, key +0x50) and takes that driver's preferred slot (driver +0xc); the others get 0,1,2... skipping it. Each entrant gets a 0x98-byte record {entrant copy, +0x88 garage, +0x90 slot} pushed to out_assignments and Sess_Set_GarageSlotEntrant_Thunk(garage, entrant, slot) (0x1424a840e, 0x1424a84ec), which ignores slot >= 2: a garage holds two cars.

name: Sess_Assign_GarageSlotsByTeamOrder
proto: void Sess_Assign_GarageSlotsByTeamOrder(void *out_assignments, void *entrants, void *garages, void *team_order, void *fixed_teams)
notes: garage index per team, called twice by Sess_Assign_GarageSlotsByClass (0x1424aadbd, 0x1424aba9d). Groups the entrants by team (Sess_Group_EntrantsByTeam_Thunk), then loop 1 walks team_order (u32 team keys: kind byte, stat id u16 at +2; e.g. the PreviousSeasonTeamStandings order): the team at list position i gets garage index i (ebp, incremented for every list entry) through Sess_Assign_GarageSlotsByPreference (0x1424a8983) with NO compare against the garage count (rdi = garage count only sizes the free list); a listed team absent from the session pushes its index to a free list unless it is in fixed_teams. Loop 2 gives each unlisted team the next index while it is below the garage count (cmp at 0x1424a8bf3), else a free index below the count (0x1424a8c2e), else no garage at all. So: a team order list longer than the world's garage vector reads past it (see Sess_Assign_GarageSlotsByPreference); teams past the garage count that are not in the list get no garage. out_assignments = {allocator, begin, end, cap} of 0x98-byte garage assignment records; *out_assignments is also the free list's allocator.

When the game message bus is active, allocates a delegate {Game_ErsSystem_HandleVehicleNewLap, self} from bus+0x78 and subscribes it under 'vehicle_newlap' (0x143987810); otherwise records errno 0x58 (bus inactive) or 0xc (no memory) in the Ne errno trace. name: Game_ErsSystem_HandleVehicleNewLap
notes: Message-bus delegate for vehicle_newlap (key string 0x14565e301), subscribed with ctx = the ERS system by Game_ErsSystem_Subscribe (delegate {fn,ctx} at 0x142517e1b) and removed by Game_ErsSystem_Unsubscribe (0x1425188fd). Walks the participant pointers self+0x30..+0x38 for the entry whose +0x28 vehicle component has +0xe8 == msg+0x10 (vehicle id); on a match with a non-null component+0x5a8 (per-car ERS state) it moves the lap's energy counters +0x19c8..+0x19d7 to +0x19dc..+0x19eb, zeroes them and +0x19d8, and sets +0x19f4 from +0x58 (mode 3), +0x50, or +0x50 + +0x54 (modes 1-2 with +0x1a61); mode = 2 if self+0x20, else 3 if self+0x21, else self+0x22. Always returns 0. Unlike Game_ErsSystem_Update it does not null-check entry+0x28, so a participant without a vehicle component (Time Trial) before the matching one faults at 0x1425180f7. Posted synchronously by the per-vehicle progress update 0x1446034b0 (Ne_Post_BusMessage at 0x144603a7e, message vtable 0x1457e6ec0 'vehicle_newlap'). EA build 0x142511450, same bytes (crash-20261027-144555).

notes: Fills the targets vector self+0x350/+0x358/+0x360 (allocator self+0x348) from the track's resource: returns at once when g_Game_TrackAcclimatisationResource is null, otherwise copies the resource's settings (+0x78..+0xd8 to self+0x388..+0x4f8) and resizes self+0x350 to the resource's CornerData vector +0x60..+0x68 (0x370-byte entries), copying each entry's gates; self+0x33c = total gate count. With no resource, or a resource whose CornerData is empty, the vector stays empty and null. Called by Game_PracticeTrackAcclimatisation_Setup when the vector is empty (0x14299cb51), and by the save-data paths 0x1429a4380 (0x1429a4683) and 0x1429a7010 (0x1429a7297). Other writers of the vector (V1187): 0x1429a7010 (slot +0x1e8) fills it from saved data when the saved count is non-zero (0x1429a716b..0x1429a72d7), slot +0x40 0x14299cc40 empties it (+0x358 = +0x350 at 0x14299cc54), the destructor 0x142a078a0 empties it (0x142a07bb3) and the ctor 0x14295f370 zeroes +0x350..+0x368.

name: Game_PracticeTrackAcclimatisation_RefreshState
notes: Track Acclimatisation practice programme (vtable vt_Game_PracticeTrackAcclimatisation, object name 'track_acclim' at +0x58): recomputes the current target from the targets vector self+0x350..+0x358 (0x370-byte entries, up to 4 corner gates of 0xd0 at +0x10, gate count at +4, flags at +0xc4/+0x194/+0x264/+0x334) and the indices +0x328/+0x7e0/+0x7e4, writes the per-gate states +0x7c0..+0x7dc and, when +0x830 is set, notifies the listeners under self+0x1d0/+0x508 and clears +0x830/+0x7fc. The entry count is never tested for zero: it reads entry [+0x7e0] at 0x14299e59b on every path, and entry [min(+0x328 - r12, count - 1)] at 0x14299e53b when +0x336 is set (r12 = 1 only with +0x334 set, +0x330 == 0 and +0x7e4 below the limit). With an empty vector (+0x350 == +0x358 == 0) it faults at 0x14299e59b (ACCESS_VIOLATION reading 0x4, community tracks in Driver Career practice as the car leaves the garage). Callers: the +0xf0 slot thunk 0x1429a0610 (tail jmp 0x1429a0617; the drive-out subscriber Game_PracticeProgramme_HandleDriveOut calls it for every programme), Game_PracticeTrackAcclimatisation_Update 0x14299e27e, and the secondary-base slot 0x1429a5bb0 (this-8) at 0x1429a5ec0; no caller reads rax. Game_PracticeTrackAcclimatisation_Start and the slot thunks 0x1429a5b70/0x1429a5b90 return when +0x358 == +0x350; this function lacks that check. .pdata 0x14299e3a0-0x14299e8a6, push r15..rbx / sub rsp,0x20 prologue (14 bytes, nothing branches into 0x14299e3a1..0x14299e3ad). EA build 0x142997720, same 0x506 bytes. Core's track acclimatisation guard returns from it when the vector is empty.

Every array path gated on +0x38/+0x39 (Game_PracticeTrackAcclimatisation_Update running branch, slot +0x180 via 0x1429532b0, 0x1429a5bb0) is therefore never reached with no targets.

name: Game_SaveSlotManager_NewSlot_Thunk
notes: thunk=0x14d6f9870 (.data1, read as disassembly on the Steam build). Allocates the 0x190-byte SaveSlotInfo from manager+0x228, copies the name into the inline buffer +0x28 (char * at +0x20, capacity 0x80 at +0x18), slot_id = next free id from manager+0x2c0 (skipping ids in use and -1, written back) under the critical section at +0x290, slot_guid = a CoCreateGuid result folded to 64 bits (0x14d6f9b66 call, 0x14d6f9b92 store) or 0 when the static at 0x14604ecc8 is null; +0x178 blob 0, +0x188 mss_id -1. The fold's on-disk bytes look mutated, so its exact form is unproven. LoadSlot (0x1429d42f0) then overwrites id and guid from the file.

name: Game_VehicleAntiStallSystem_Update
notes: per-car race start / anti-stall state machine (entry+0x18 0..3), logs '[VEHICLE RACE START] sending Race Start message for vehicle id: %d reaction time: %.3f'; while system+0x100 == 0 it sets bit 2 in the car input block (+0x50 -> +0x1fc) and clears it otherwise; system pointer also at [0x146095a68]. name: Game_VehicleAntiStallSystem_Init
notes: VehicleAntiStallSystem init: subscribes MessageRaceStarted (0x142f4ec50), MessageVehicleLeftGarage (0x142f4ed60), RollingStartMessage (0x142f4eed0), MessageStartLightOn (0x142f4f040, sets +0x104 = lights) and RedFlagStatusChangedMessage (0x142f4f050 -> .data1 0x14f8e7290). Per-car entries at +0x48..+0x50 (entry+0x18 start state 0..3, +0x30, +0x50 vehicle with +0x9f18). (vmknolle red-flag-pit)

name: Game_VehicleAntiStallSystem_OnRaceStarted
notes: MessageRaceStarted subscriber (Denuvo thunk, emulated offline): +0x104 = 0, +0x109 = 1 (lights out), +0x100 = 1 (start hold off), +0x110 = 0, +0x114 = 1, +0x118 = 0, resets every car entry (+0x18..+0x3c, vehicle +0x9f18).

name: Game_VehicleAntiStallSystem_OnVehicleLeftGarage
notes: MessageVehicleLeftGarage subscriber (emulated): resets the entry of car msg+0x10, entry +0x30 = 1.

name: Game_VehicleAntiStallSystem_OnRollingStart
notes: RollingStartMessage subscriber (emulated): same per-car reset as OnVehicleLeftGarage.

name: Game_VehicleAntiStallSystem_OnStartLightOn
notes: MessageStartLightOn subscriber (emulated): +0x104 = msg+0x10 (lights on).

name: Game_VehicleAntiStallSystem_OnRedFlagStatus_Thunk
notes: thunk to the Denuvo body 0x14f8e7290. Emulated offline (Unicorn, checked against the plain VehicleLeftGarage handler): status != 2 does nothing; status 2 writes the same system fields as the MessageRaceStarted handler (+0x104 = 0, +0x109 = 1, +0x100 = 1, +0x110 = 0, +0x114 = 1); the per-car loop could not be emulated (runtime-decrypted constants). (vmknolle red-flag-pit)

name: Game_Network_SetScenario
proto: void Game_Network_SetScenario(void *session, uint8_t stat_id, const void *spec)
notes: Logs 'setScenario: scenarioStatId: %d, specRaceVehicleStatId: %s' and 'setGameSetupMode: gameSetupModeStatId: %d'. Returns early when session+0x410 already holds stat_id and the 4-byte spec matches (+0x18, valid flag +0x1c; default spec 0x3fff0000). Else stores stat_id at +0x410 and spec at +0x18, finds the scenario row (g_Game_Scenarios entries, stat id byte +0, game setup mode byte +0x18, entrant list +0x20), applies that setup mode's entrants, marks the session dirty (+0x766/+0x768 and the send thunk 0x143227630) and, when session+8 == 1 (host), sends the scenario to clients. setupFromUnranked ends with it (the scenario whose name equals the category value), session = *(*(self+0x10)+0x418).

name: Car_Upgrades_CalcNonLinearMass
notes: (Upgrades team model, owner). linear = sum over type metadata records (+0x1a38..+0x1a40 stride 0x20) of Car_Upgrades_CalcTypeMass; total = sum of the records' mass at full (+4); f = linear/total; returns linear + f*(f*target - linear) with target = Upgrades+0x50 ('Target mass at max'). Log channel VEHICLE_UPGRADES_MASS. Callers 0x142f5a5d0 (car mass for a pace/strategy estimate: fuel FuelTank+0x100 + Chassis Mass + this) and 0x142962f10 (garage/programme UI). proto: void*(void *uitc, void *tab_node, const char *key, void *point, uint8_t visible, int64_t header_index)
notes: UITC (tab controller) adds one tab: reads the tab entry key (content_template / header_template) from the tabs[i] VM node, formats the instance name tab_<n>( <tpl> ), looks the template up (miss at 0x144267110 -> returns NULL silently) and instantiates it under the UITC node; instance rc checked at 0x14426708d (non-zero -> returns NULL silently; a descendant failure leaves the partial tree attached, a root init failure attaches nothing). name: Gdb_Load_GameDatabase
notes: Constructs and loads the game value database (strings gamedatabases.bin, GameDatabase.fileName, GAME_VALUE_DB, GDB databasePath). Writes db->vtable 0x145bee5d0, builds the record allocator at db+8 (vtable 0x145bee810, named GVDB_READ_ONLY_REDIRECT, forwards to the GAME_VALUE_DB heap at db+0x90), initialises the empty value map at db+0xa8 (0x1445a04dd..0x1445a0535: mult 0xc4ceb9fe1a85ec53, keyvals=info=&mask, count=mask=max=0, info_inc 0x20), sets g_Gdb_Database (0x1445a053e) and g_Gdb_RecordAllocator=db+8 (0x1445a0562). Loads the file into a buffer (u32 record count, then records {u64 key, u8 tag, u32 len, text[len], nul}), reserves the map for max(count, map.num_elements) at site_Gdb_ReserveTarget -> Gdb_HashMap_Rehash (0x1445a0aa3), inserts every record with Gdb_HashMap_Insert (0x1445a0c3b no text, 0x1445a0e17 text unscrambled in place), sets db->loaded (+0xf0)=1 (0x1445a0f41). Core inline-hooks it (gamedb.cpp S_LOAD). Its entry is too early to size the map: the init above overwrites the map fields

name: Gdb_HashMap_Insert
proto: void Gdb_HashMap_Insert(GdbDatabase *db, uint64_t key, uint8_t tag, char *text)
notes: Inserts or updates one record in db->map (robin_hood insert_move inlined). Callers: only Gdb_Load_GameDatabase's two record loops, plus the core's gamedb.cpp edits. Probes as Gdb_Lookup_Key; a new key takes a slot (count++, value 0), then the tag switch (jump table 0x145bee930, tags 0..0x12) parses text into the existing record or allocates one from g_Gdb_RecordAllocator vt+0x18; returns the record. Growth (increase_size) before placing a new key: mask 0 -> 8 buckets; count >= max_num_elements_allowed, or an info overflow with info_inc < 3 -> Gdb_HashMap_Rehash at site_Gdb_InsertGrowCall (2*(mask+1), or the same size with mult += 0xc4ceb9fe1a85ec54 when count*2 < max); otherwise info_inc halves in place (try_increase_info, no rehash). 256 failed growth rounds -> overflow fatal 0x1445a66b0. Growth after records exist frees them all (Gdb_HashMap_Rehash), so an insert of a new key at count = max_num_elements_allowed (838,860 for 2^20 slots) leaves dangling records and the next reader crashes. Corrects the exe-agent note that the map grows safely

name: Gdb_Get_FieldInt

notes: Field lookup: builds '<rowpath>.<field>', FNV-1a-64, probes the global robin_hood map (martinus v3: mult 0xc4ceb9fe1a85ec53 @+0xb8, keyvals +0xc0, info +0xc8, size +0xd0, mask +0xd8, maxAllowed +0xe0, infoInc +0xe8, shift +0xec) and returns &entry.value. notes: Calls 0x145351784 and traps (int3); never returns. Called where robin_hood throws its overflow error: the load's reserve when the power-of-two search wraps to 0 (0x1445a11c3), Gdb_HashMap_Insert after 256 growth rounds (0x1445a2078), Gdb_HashMap_Rehash when an info overflow hits info_inc < 3 while re-inserting (0x1445a6ccb)

name: Gdb_HashMap_Rehash
notes: martinus robin_hood Table::rehashPowerOfTwo for the GVDB value map (its only two callers: the load's reserve 0x1445a0aa3 and Gdb_HashMap_Insert's growth 0x1445a1325). num_buckets must be a power of two >= 8: sets mask=num_buckets-1, max_num_elements_allowed=num_buckets*80/100, count=0, info_inc=0x20, allocates (num_buckets+min(max,0xff))*17+8 bytes from map->allocator vt+0x10 (slots 16 B each, then info bytes; null -> fatal 0x1403139f0), then re-inserts every old slot. GAME BUG: each moved slot is copied (0x1445a6bd1..0x1445a6bd6) and then the old record is destroyed (record vt+8, flag 0, 0x1445a6c09) and freed through g_Gdb_RecordAllocator vt+0x38 (0x1445a6c1b), so after a rehash of a map that holds records every slot points at freed memory.
